results.content:
SurveyMonkey — Your best decisions start with listening

SurveyMonkey now asks your customers questions in conversation, the way a person actually would, and hands the answers back already analysed. Nobody fills in a grid of radio buttons voluntarily. It benchmarks your numbers against companies in your space, so you find out whether your score is good or quietly terrible, and it plugs into ChatGPT and Slack so the feedback lands where you already argue about things, with no research team to hire and no fieldwork to wait on.

Captain Kill Switch — Close all your open apps in one click [...] Captain Kill Switch is one button in your menu bar that closes every running app. Simon Crean built it after the same stupid moment kept repeating, finishing for the day with thirty-odd windows open and shutting them one at a time, which he describes as tidying a room by picking up individual grains of rice. No dashboard, no settings, no account. Anything still open a couple of seconds later gets force-closed, unsaved work and all, and he says that on the launch page rather than letting you find out on a Friday evening, which is the right way round.

Title: MacQuit for Mac | Quit, Force Quit, and Manage Running Apps
# MacQuit. ## Quit, force quit, and reset a crowded Mac workspace faster. MacQuit is built for the moment when your Mac is full of open apps, background tools, and one-off windows you no longer need. Instead of quitting each app one by one, you get a single menu bar control for closing everything quickly and getting back to a clean desktop. The app also goes further than a simple quit-all shortcut. You can force quit frozen apps, review CPU and memory usage before closing processes, keep specific apps out of the quit list, and auto-close idle apps when you want your Mac to stay lean throughout the day. ### Quit all apps, instantly. Select what to quit with checkboxes, then hit Quit All. Your running apps are listed with real-time CPU and memory stats. ### Force quit when you need to. Hold Option to switch every button to Force Quit. Force quit when you need to. ### Find any app, fast. Real-time search filters your running apps as you type. Instantly find the app you're looking for, even with dozens running. ### Auto-quit idle apps. Apps unused longer than your threshold get quit automatically. Quit all apps from anywhere with a keyboard shortcut. Protect music apps from being quit. Answers to the questions people usually ask before trying a quit-all app on macOS. ### How do I quit all apps on Mac at once? MacQuit puts your running apps in a menu bar panel so you can select what to close and quit everything with one click, instead of opening each app and quitting it manually. ### Can MacQuit force quit frozen apps? Yes. If an app is stuck, MacQuit can switch into force quit mode so you can close unresponsive apps without going through Activity Monitor. ### Does MacQuit help manage resource-heavy apps? Yes. MacQuit shows CPU and memory usage next to running apps, which makes it easier to spot apps that are chewing through system resources. Yes. MacQuit is a native macOS alternative designed around one-click quitting, force quit support, auto-quit rules, and a simple one-time license. © 2026 Awesome Mac App. All rights reserved.
